question: By selling an item for ₹222, a person incurs a loss of ₹48. What is the percentage of loss incurred in the transaction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹222 and **Loss** = ₹48.

Calculate **Cost Price (CP)** = SP + Loss = 222 + 48 = ₹270.

Loss percentage is calculated on **Cost Price**.

Loss% = (48 ÷ 270) × 100 = (8 ÷ 45) × 100 = 800 ÷ 45 = 160 ÷ 9 = 17 7/9%.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 7/9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP = ₹222, Loss = ₹48.

**Formulas:** CP = SP + Loss | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd385b5f316f162e1e3b471fa5c657b46fa37b3b906a79cbbe7e465f1f65ca9b.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 222 + 48 = ₹270

⇒ **Loss%** = (48 ÷ 270) × 100

⇒ **Loss%** = (16 ÷ 90) × 100 = 160 ÷ 9 = 17 7/9%

**∴ The correct answer is 17 7/9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss and Cost Price Relationship

When an item is sold at a loss, the **Cost Price** is always greater than the **Selling Price**. CP = SP + Loss.

Percentage Calculation

Profit or Loss percentages are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specifically stated otherwise in the problem.
